title: LatentLoop: Scaling Looped MoE Models with Asymmetric Compute Allocation
excerpt: Looped Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models combine parameter reuse with sparse computation to improve performance under matched budgets. Prior work demonstrates that different loop visits can play different roles even when they share parameters. To probe the contributions of different loop visits, we learn separate residual coefficients in a model that applies a shared block twice, observing a smaller scale in the first visit. Fixed coefficient experiments show that reducing the first visit's scale preserves or improves performance, whereas the same reductions to the second hurt it. This asymmetry motivates us to explore asymmetric compute allocation. We propose LatentLoop, which compresses the…

ai.summary: LatentLoop proposes a looped Mixture‑of‑Experts architecture that applies a shared block twice with asymmetric compute allocation, learning separate residual coefficients for each loop visit to improve efficiency under fixed budgets.
ai.why: The technique offers a way to boost model performance without increasing total compute, useful for scaling MoE models in production.

title: Plan or Retrieve First? A Scale Study of Tool Discovery Architectures
excerpt: Tool-augmented LLM agents discover relevant APIs from large registries before planning execution, yet finite context windows prohibit injecting all tool definitions into a single prompt. The dominant approach, which we term Retrieve-then-Plan (RtP), embeds the user query and retrieves similar tools via approximate nearest-neighbor search. We study an alternative Plan-then-Retrieve (PtR) paradigm in which the LLM first generates Abstract Tool Stubs (hypothesized function signatures describing needed capabilities) which then serve as retrieval queries against the registry. Evaluating on…

ai.summary: Apple studied a Plan‑then‑Retrieve (PtR) architecture for tool‑augmented LLM agents, where the LLM first generates abstract tool stubs before retrieving relevant APIs, contrasting the common Retrieve‑then‑Plan (RtP) approach.
ai.why: It offers a new strategy for API discovery that may reduce context‑window usage in agent design.

title: KV4-RL: Unlocking Faster Asynchronous Rollouts for RLVR with INT4 KV Cache Quantization
excerpt: Asynchronous rollout improves the efficiency of reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) by reducing under-utilization during long-tail generation. Sustained concurrency also concentrates context processing into fewer decode steps, increasing the KV workload per step. We characterize this KV concentration and find that KV cache quantization delivers substantially greater acceleration than weight-only and weight-activation quantization in our matched-workload comparisons. However, INT4 KV rollout can degrade learning even with token-level truncated importance sampling (TIS). We propose KV4-RL, which combines calibration-free INT4 KV quantization with selective INT8 protection of…

ai.summary: KV4‑RL demonstrates that INT4 quantization of the KV cache accelerates asynchronous rollout in reinforcement‑learning‑with‑verifiable‑rewards (RLVR) more than weight‑only or weight‑activation quantization.
ai.why: Developers can speed up RL training pipelines by applying low‑bit KV cache quantization to reduce latency.

title: Seeing, Maintaining, and Learning: The Evolution of Multimodal Agent Memory
excerpt: Multimodal models and agents have emerged to enable AI systems to learn from and interact with the real world more like humans by integrating information across multiple modalities. However, enabling multimodal agents to continually acquire useful information from complex, heterogeneous multimodal data remains a significant challenge as they move toward long-horizon tasks and lifelong settings. Addressing this challenge requires effective memory mechanisms that can maintain continuity across sessions, adapt to changing users and environments, and refine memory-management policies through accumulated experience. We introduce a two-axis analytical framework for multimodal agent memory…

ai.summary: The work surveys and proposes memory mechanisms for multimodal agents to continuously acquire and retain information across heterogeneous data streams for long‑horizon and lifelong tasks.
ai.why: Improved memory designs can help developers build agents that retain context over extended interactions, enhancing usability in real‑world applications.

title: Towards Agentic Robots: Model, Data, Environment, and Harness
excerpt: Foundation models are driving a paradigm shift in robotic intelligence, moving beyond low-level action prediction to goal-directed orchestration of data collection, model training, task planning, and real-world execution. We characterize this emerging paradigm as an agentic robots, in which agents reason over human instructions, interact with robotic environments, rectify execution errors autonomously, and dynamically adjust operational strategies. Although this field develops fast, current studies are not well connected. Researchers have no consistent view of how to combine different agentic functions into a complete robot system. This paper provides a unified overview of existing research…

ai.summary: The paper outlines an “agentic robots” paradigm where foundation models orchestrate data collection, model training, planning, and execution, handling error correction and strategy adjustment autonomously.
ai.why: Guides developers toward building more self‑sufficient robotic agents that go beyond low‑level control.

title: More Methods, Better Agents? A Reality Check on Self-Distillation in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
excerpt: Self-distillation in agentic reinforcement learning has produced a growing number of methods. However, existing evaluations often reuse published baseline scores under differing experimental conditions, provide few direct comparisons among contemporaneous methods, and give limited attention to training stability and computational cost. These limitations obscure the source of reported gains and the practical strengths and weaknesses of competing methods. Costly agent training further motivates a common basis for comparison. To address these gaps, we compare ten representative methods against GRPO on ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, Search-QA, and WebShop across three model sizes. Our study comprises…

ai.summary: The study conducts a reality check on self‑distillation methods in agentic reinforcement learning, comparing training stability, computational cost, and actual performance gains across recent approaches.
ai.why: Provides developers with clearer guidance on which self‑distillation techniques are practically beneficial versus costly.

title: Super-Resolution in The Right Latent Space: A Frozen Vision-Foundation Substrate
excerpt: In an image latent space, the embeddings of high-resolution, natural, and sharp images form a manifold. Degradation of high-resolution images pushes their embeddings off this manifold. Real-world super-resolution (SR) then becomes the task of mapping the degraded embedding back onto this manifold --- not anywhere on the manifold, but to the point that preserves what the input still carries, both its semantics and pixel details. Every published method implements this mapping in a reconstruction-oriented latent space or pixel space. We claim these spaces are the wrong substrates for SR. Low-resolution and degraded images are embedded far from the manifold, making the mapping difficult and…

ai.summary: The paper "Super-Resolution in The Right Latent Space" proposes using a frozen vision‑foundation model as a latent substrate to map degraded image embeddings back onto the high‑resolution manifold for super‑resolution.
ai.why: Provides a new approach that could improve image SR quality without training full end‑to‑end models.

title: Doc2Harness: Benchmarking LLMs on Long-Horizon Harness Engineering of Coding Agents
excerpt: Agents driven by large language models are increasingly deployed on long-horizon tasks, where they use tools and modify real workspaces. How well they perform depends as much on the harness around the model as on the model itself. Existing benchmarks measure downstream task success under a fixed harness, leaving harness engineering itself unexplored. We propose Doc2Harness, a two-stage benchmark that evaluates long-horizon harness engineering directly. In Stage 1, a build model operating inside a fixed builder harness receives an interface-only contract skeleton and a development document that consolidates behavior across twelve frontier harnesses, and then constructs a complete candidate…

ai.summary: Doc2Harness introduces a two‑stage benchmark that evaluates both the performance of LLM‑driven coding agents and the quality of the surrounding harness that manages long‑horizon tasks.
ai.why: Helps developers assess and improve the integration layer that enables LLMs to execute complex coding workflows.

title: Any Time, Any Space: A World-State-Centric Framework for Agentic Video Generation
excerpt: Long-form agentic video generation must turn a screenplay into shots that remain spatially and temporally consistent across nonconsecutive requests. Passing prompts or recent frames between shots does not provide a shared spatial frame for revisiting a scene or a time-indexed record for replaying an earlier event. We present Any Time, Any Space (ATAS), which compiles a screenplay into shot requests with explicit location, camera, and event-time references. Before generation, it retrieves relevant evidence from a scene memory of registered static geometry and an event memory of dynamic observations indexed by scene, event, and time. After generation, ATAS reconstructs and registers the clip…

ai.summary: The paper introduces Any Time, Any Space (ATAS), a framework that converts a screenplay into shot requests with explicit location, camera, and event-time references to ensure spatial and temporal consistency in long‑form agentic video generation.
ai.why: It provides a structured approach developers can use to build video generation agents that maintain continuity across non‑consecutive prompts.

title: RAR: Rate-Adaptive Rollout for Time-Consistent Interactive World Models
excerpt: Video-based interactive world models aim to enable real-time, user-controllable environments. Yet most existing systems are trained and rolled out at a fixed temporal rate, limiting both runtime-rate adaptation and physical-horizon coverage -- a limitation we term temporal-rate coupling. Specifically, when runtime generation throughput differs from the learned temporal rate, the generated world evolves unintentionally more slowly or quickly. Moreover, using a single temporal rate imposes an inherent trade-off between temporal granularity and physical horizon: higher rates capture finer motion but cover a shorter duration under a fixed context window. To address both limitations, we…

ai.summary: The paper proposes Rate-Adaptive Rollout (RAR), a method that lets interactive video world models adjust their generation speed at runtime to match varying temporal rates, reducing temporal-rate coupling and extending physical-horizon coverage.
ai.why: It enables developers to build more responsive, real‑time simulation environments without retraining models for each speed.

title: Cortex: Consolidating Context into Parametric Memory
excerpt: Context can improve large language model performance, but these gains may be lost after context removal. Inspired by biological systems consolidation, we formulate Memory Consolidation (MC) as internalizing these gains while preserving non-target capabilities, connecting context-specified editing, skill learning, and behavioral steering under a common objective. We introduce a five-task-family testbed measuring consolidation and retention under single, batch, and sequential updates. We propose Cortex, which generates prospective queries to anticipate uses of context and distills context-conditioned outputs into mergeable low-rank or structural feed-forward network updates. Across 4B--120B…

ai.summary: The paper "Cortex: Consolidating Context into Parametric Memory" proposes Memory Consolidation to internalize context gains in LLMs, preserving performance after context removal, and introduces a five‑task testbed for evaluating consolidation and retention.
ai.why: Offers a method to make LLMs retain learned context without needing long prompts, useful for building more efficient agents.

title: Many Right Answers, One Training Example: Removing Responder Noise from GRPO for LLM Recommenders
excerpt: A recommendation request on Reddit draws several replies, each naming different titles. When an LLM recommender is trained on such threads with reinforcement learning (RL), which replies should a generated list be rewarded against? The state-of-the-art recipe, Rank-GRPO, picks one reply per training example, so the advantage mostly records which reply was drawn (85% of its variance) rather than how good the list is. We argue that RL should train on the request, not on each answer, and propose ReMaRk: it scores every list once against the union of all replies' titles and samples each request equally. This makes RL cheaper. On seven backbones and three datasets, ReMaRk reaches the validation…

ai.summary: The paper identifies that Rank-GRPO, a state-of-the-art RL recipe for LLM recommenders, suffers from high variance (85%) because it rewards generated lists against a single sampled reply rather than the original request. The authors propose a method to remove this 'responder noise' by training on the request context, ensuring the advantage signal reflects list quality rather than which specific reply was drawn.
ai.why: Relevant for developers building RL-based recommendation systems, as it offers a concrete fix for a common training instability issue in GRPO implementations.

title: LensErase: A Foundation Model for Erase Anything
excerpt: We introduce LensErase, a general-purpose mask-based Erase Anything foundation model designed to cover a broad spectrum of real-world erase scenarios. LensErase supports diverse objects, visual text, watermarks, associated visual effects, multiple-object removal, and a wide range of object scales, aspect ratios, and image resolutions. First, to enable such broad coverage, we construct LensErase-100M, a large-scale dataset containing 101.07 million paired source-mask-target examples spanning diverse erase scenarios. Second, we pretrain LensErase from the text-to-image model Lens, adapting its strong generative prior to mask-based erasing. To efficiently incorporate the source image and erase…

ai.summary: LensErase is a foundation model trained on a 101 M image‑mask‑target dataset to perform mask‑based erasing of objects, text, watermarks, and visual effects across varied scales and resolutions.
ai.why: Developers can integrate LensErase for robust content removal in image editing pipelines without needing task‑specific fine‑tuning.

title: RuleTrek: Benchmarking Agentic Rule Reasoning in Complex Scenarios
excerpt: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly tackle complex real-world tasks in specialized domains. However, identifying and correctly applying domain-specific rules remains challenging when scenario information is distributed across multiple files. Existing rule-reasoning benchmarks typically represent scenarios using only a few factual statements, simplifying the identification and application of relevant rules. To address this gap, this paper introduces RuleTrek, a multi-domain benchmark for agentic rule reasoning in complex scenarios. Its rule-grounded construction pipeline extracts structured rule graphs, generates and incrementally composes rule-specific sub-scenarios while ensuring…

ai.summary: The paper introduces RuleTrek, a multi-domain benchmark that evaluates large language models' ability to identify and apply domain-specific rules when relevant information is spread across multiple files.
ai.why: It provides a more realistic test for agents that need to reason over complex, distributed data, helping developers gauge and improve rule-based capabilities.

title: Beyond Domain-Routed Supervision: Cross-Teacher Guarding for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
excerpt: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) extends on-policy distillation (OPD) by routing domain-specific data to specialized teachers, integrating their capabilities through dense token-level supervision on student-generated trajectories. However, domain routing only distinguishes the supervision sources for different domains; updates from all domains still act on shared parameters. When teachers differ substantially in response style and domain expertise, supervision that is effective in isolation may still lead to persistent gradient conflicts and capability degradation during joint optimization. To address this challenge, we propose Cross-Teacher Guarding for MOPD (Road MOPD), which…

ai.summary: The paper presents Cross‑Teacher Guarding, a technique for multi‑teacher on‑policy distillation that adds token‑level supervision from multiple specialized teachers while guarding against conflicting updates.
ai.why: It enables developers to distill diverse expertise into a single student model more safely, improving performance on multi‑domain tasks.

excerpt: Multimodal agents commonly generate freeform reasoning before each action. SSR represents recurring high-level reasoning as pre-specified, reusable natural-language candidates. At each turn, the model selects from the reasoning candidates based on their…

ai.summary: Apple researchers introduced Selection‑based Structured Reasoning (SSR), a framework that turns multimodal agent reasoning into a selection task rather than open‑ended generation, aiming to reduce inference cost for small models.

title: Recovering Reliable Supervision via Critique-Guided On-Policy Distillation
excerpt: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student model on its own rollouts with token-level supervision from a teacher, assuming that the teacher can reach a correct answer from any prefix the student writes. We call this property the recoverability of the teacher and show it fails on incorrect rollouts: the teacher follows student errors, although it recognizes them. We propose CriticOPD, using error recognition to restore recoverability. The teacher critiques an incorrect rollout, allowing the student to rewrite its solution following the error. The resulting output, including the critique as privileged information, is scored by the teacher while the student uses the revision without the…

ai.summary: CriticOPD extends on‑policy distillation by having the teacher critique incorrect student rollouts, restoring recoverability and providing better supervision for error correction.
ai.why: The approach can be used to train more reliable language models that self‑correct during generation, beneficial for developer‑facing assistants.

title: SwarmRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Scientific Agent Swarm
excerpt: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) in scientific research aims to improve agents' research capabilities through their own experimental experience. Scientific agent swarms can combine evidence and implementations from different research directions to guide their agents' subsequent experiments. However, poor experimental results can leave unclear whether to revise a hypothesis or its implementation, while overall program scores can hide components useful to other agents. To address these challenges, we introduce SwarmRSI, a framework that evolves scientific agent swarms for recursive self-improvement. We devise Feedback-Guided Swarm Mutation to refine hypotheses and their implementations using…

ai.summary: SwarmRSI presents a framework for recursive self‑improvement in scientific research by evolving a swarm of agents that share experimental results and implementations to guide subsequent experiments.
ai.why: Shows a potential pathway for autonomous research agents to iteratively enhance their own capabilities.

title: ActionOPD: Distilling Decisions, Not Tokens
excerpt: Distilling capable language-model agents into smaller models requires aligning the student's behavior with the teacher's. This raises a fundamental question: at which states and at what granularity should this alignment be performed? Offline imitation provides dense but token-specific supervision and can suffer from state-distribution mismatch. Token-level on-policy distillation (OPD) addresses this mismatch but typically requires teacher token probabilities and compatible tokenization. We argue that semantic actions provide a natural unit of supervision for agent distillation. We introduce ActionOPD, an action-level on-policy distillation method motivated by maximizing expected…

ai.summary: "ActionOPD: Distilling Decisions, Not Tokens" presents token‑level on‑policy distillation that aligns student agents with teacher behavior without requiring teacher token probabilities, addressing state‑distribution mismatch in imitation learning.
ai.why: Enables smaller language‑model agents to inherit decision‑making abilities of larger teachers more efficiently.

We extend the computer-use action space with relative pointer motion, sustained inputs…

title: HumanoidToolBench: Benchmarking Humanoid Tool Use from Selection to Mobile Execution
excerpt: As robotic hardware and learning methods advance, humanoids need tools to perform tasks beyond their inherent physical limits. Evaluation of seven policies in simulation and three on the real robot reveals substantial gaps between selecting a suitable…

title: Hybrid Reasoning Agents
excerpt: How can we build an agent that thinks beyond human language, yet still acts through it in the external environment? Modern LLM agents still reason and interact through text, while latent reasoning offers an efficient internal medium but lacks native tool access and reasoning transparency. We bridge these two directions with Hybrid Reasoning Agents (HybridAgents), which dynamically navigate between latent reasoning and text-based interaction throughout a unified generation process. Architecturally, a lightweight HybridLink enables seamless transitions between text and latent modes, while the agent's continuous working memory preserves lossless hybrid context across multiple turns. These…

title: CLASHarness: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Conflict in Computer Use via a Controllable and Verifiable Generation Pipeline
excerpt: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly deployed in multi-agent systems to automate complex computer-use workflows, yet existing benchmarks mostly assume consistent, cooperative environments. In contrast, real-world collaboration rarely runs on consistent information: peer or sub-agents frequently report outdated states, issue contradictory instructions, or compete over shared permissions and files, forcing agents to check others' outputs and verify ground truth in the environment. Evaluating such conflict resolution remains challenging: manual authoring cannot scale across complex systems, while unconstrained LLM generation produces narrative drift, answer leakage, and unsatisfiable…

ai.summary: The paper introduces CLASHarness, a benchmark for evaluating vision-language models in multi-agent computer-use scenarios where agents face conflicting instructions, outdated states, or permission conflicts.
ai.why: Useful for developers building robust multi-agent systems, as it provides a testbed for handling real-world inconsistencies and verification challenges in automated workflows.
